verdict.rationale: Better Auth's own MCP plugin lets an app act as an OAuth authorization server and protected resource for MCP clients, which directly addresses putting OAuth in front of an MCP server. The homepage also advertises MCP auth for agents, and the separate JWT plugin offers JWKS-verifiable tokens. However, the evidence never documents scope handling or specific MCP-spec compliance details, and the JWKS verification is not tied to the MCP plugin. missing for 10: documented token scoping for MCP clients, explicit spec-compliance details (e.g. discovery metadata, client registration), evidence that MCP-issued tokens are verifiable via JWKS, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can put a spec-compliant OAuth authorization flow in front of my MCP server so remote agents connect with scoped, verifiable tokens

citations.quote: The MCP plugin lets your app act as an OAuth authorization server and protected resource for Model Context Protocol clients.
Auth for AI agents. MCP auth, token exchange, and agent delegation.
The JWT plugin provides endpoints to retrieve a JWT token and a JWKS endpoint to verify the token.
